title: Deterministic synthesis and processing of frequency-bin qubits in a macroscopically coherent quantum memory
abstract: Quantum information processing requires efficient storage and manipulation of photonic states.Here, we advance a cavity-assisted quantum memory protocol based on Pre-created Long-lived Macroscopic (PLM) coherence, thereby transforming quantum memory from a passive storage device into a platform for deterministic in-memory photonic processing. It is demonstrated that spin PLM coherence enables all-optical control of quantum memory using robust radio-frequency rotations alone. Here, the spin coherence serves as a distributed coherent quantum bus, which mediates the deterministic synthesis and storage of frequency-bin states through spectrally nonlocal impedance matching. We identify an inherent time-reversal symmetry in the underlying dynamical equations, ensuring unitary evolution of the quantum memory operations. The presented results demonstrate a unified platform for quantum storage and optical signal processing, enabling controlled manipulation of frequency-bin photonic qubits and paving the way for scalable multimode quantum networks based on spectral-encoding architectures.
summary: This work details a protocol to transform quantum memory in REI-doped crystals into an active quantum processor for photonic qubits. By leveraging spin PLM coherence, the authors show how to deterministically synthesize frequency-bin qubits using cavity-assisted techniques. This establishes a unified platform for both quantum storage and advanced optical signal processing.
main_problem: The paper aims to advance quantum memory from a passive storage device to an active platform capable of deterministically processing photonic states, specifically frequency-bin qubits.
main_result: The use of spin Pre-created Long-lived Macroscopic (PLM) coherence enables all-optical control and the deterministic synthesis of frequency-bin qubits via spectrally nonlocal impedance matching.
method: The analysis employs the input-output formalism and solves coupled differential equations derived from the system Hamiltonian, analyzing the resulting echo fields in the frequency domain.
model_or_system: The system is a cavity-assisted quantum memory utilizing Rare-Earth Ion (REI) doped crystals, where the dynamics are governed by the interaction between cavity modes and multiple spin coherences.
key_observables: Output echo fields ($	ilde{a}_{2,3;out}(\omega)$) and the ability to synthesize frequency-bin photonic qubits.
important_parameters: The generalized spectrally nonlocal impedance-matching condition ($\alpha_{22}\langle\hat{S}_{22}angle/\kappa_2 + \alpha_{33}\langle\hat{S}_{33}angle/\kappa_3 = 1/2$) and the spin PLM coherence ($\hat{S}_{23}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a narrow input bandwidth ($\delta\omega_s$) and neglects the effect of the weak signal pulse on the populations of the atomic states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the atomic energy levels, the timing sequence of control pulses (RF and $\pi$-lasers), and the schematic setup involving the REI-doped crystal in a dual-mode resonator.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by first defining the system dynamics using coupled equations, then solving these in the frequency domain using the input-output formalism, and finally deriving the conditions necessary for deterministic frequency-bin qubit synthesis.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical blueprint for using solid-state quantum memories not just for storage, but as an active processor for complex photonic quantum states, which is a major goal in quantum networking.
